title: The Endocrine System
status: upcoming — may be end of A&P 1 or start of A&P 2

endocrine_vs_nervous.endocrine: HORMONES via BLOOD. slow onset (seconds to hours). long-lasting effects (hours to weeks). widespread targets. chemical messengers.
endocrine_vs_nervous.nervous: NEUROTRANSMITTERS via SYNAPSES. fast onset (milliseconds). brief effects (milliseconds). specific targets. electrical + chemical signals.
endocrine_vs_nervous.overlap: hypothalamus bridges both. neuroendocrine cells release hormones. some chemicals serve as BOTH NT and hormone (NE, epinephrine).

amino_acid_based.types: amines (modified amino acids: epinephrine, NE, thyroid hormones, melatonin), peptides (short chains: ADH, oxytocin), proteins (longer chains: GH, insulin, PTH)
amino_acid_based.mechanism: WATER-SOLUBLE (except thyroid hormones). can't cross membrane. bind SURFACE RECEPTORS → activate SECOND MESSENGER system (usually cAMP).
second_messenger_cAMP: 1. hormone binds receptor on cell surface
6. protein kinases phosphorylate enzymes → cellular response
amino_acid_based.characteristics: FAST acting. short-lived. can't be stored in blood long (degraded quickly). travel FREE in blood (water-soluble).

steroid_hormones.what: made from CHOLESTEROL. sex hormones (estrogen, progesterone, testosterone) + adrenal cortex hormones (cortisol, aldosterone).
steroid_hormones.mechanism: LIPID-SOLUBLE. cross cell membrane freely. bind INTRACELLULAR RECEPTORS (usually in nucleus). hormone-receptor complex acts as TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR → activates/deactivates genes → new protein synthesis.
steroid_hormones.characteristics: SLOW acting (hours). long-lasting (change gene expression). travel in blood BOUND TO CARRIER PROTEINS (albumin, specific binding globulins). only FREE hormone is active.

hormone_chemistry.thyroid_hormones: amino acid-based BUT behave like steroids — lipid-soluble, cross membrane, bind intracellular receptors. the exception.

negative_feedback.what: MOST COMMON. output inhibits further input. maintains homeostasis.
negative_feedback.example_thyroid: hypothalamus → TRH → anterior pituitary → TSH → thyroid → T3/T4. when T3/T4 rises → inhibits hypothalamus (less TRH) + inhibits anterior pituitary (less TSH) → thyroid output decreases.
negative_feedback.example_blood_glucose: high glucose → pancreas beta cells → insulin → cells absorb glucose → glucose drops → insulin secretion stops.

positive_feedback.what: RARE. output AMPLIFIES input. runs to completion, then stops.
positive_feedback.examples: oxytocin during labor (contractions → oxytocin → stronger contractions → more oxytocin → until birth). blood clotting cascade. LH surge triggering ovulation.

hormone_regulation.humoral: hormone release in response to changing blood levels of ions/nutrients. EX: Ca2+ levels directly stimulate parathyroid.
hormone_regulation.neural: nerve fibers stimulate hormone release. EX: sympathetic stimulation → adrenal medulla → epinephrine.
hormone_regulation.hormonal: hormone stimulates another endocrine gland. EX: anterior pituitary hormones (TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH) stimulate target glands.

hypothalamus.role: MASTER of the master gland. controls anterior pituitary via RELEASING and INHIBITING HORMONES carried through hypophyseal portal system.
hypothalamus.releasing_hormones: TRH (→ TSH), CRH (→ ACTH), GnRH (→ FSH + LH), GHRH (→ GH)
hypothalamus.also_makes: oxytocin + ADH — stored in + released from POSTERIOR pituitary. hypothalamus MAKES them, posterior pituitary STORES + RELEASES them.

anterior_pituitary.what: adenohypophysis. TRUE endocrine gland (makes its own hormones). controlled by hypothalamic releasing/inhibiting hormones via hypophyseal portal system.

GH_growth_hormone.effects: stimulates growth. liver produces IGF-1 (insulin-like growth factor) which mediates most effects. increases protein synthesis, fat breakdown, blood glucose.
GH_growth_hormone.hyper: children: gigantism. adults: acromegaly (enlarged hands, feet, face).

ACTH_adrenocorticotropic.effect: stimulates cortisol (+ some aldosterone + androgens) release

FSH_follicle_stimulating.effect: females: stimulates follicle development + estrogen production. males: stimulates sperm production (spermatogenesis) in Sertoli cells.

LH_luteinizing.effect: females: triggers ovulation, maintains corpus luteum → progesterone. males: stimulates testosterone production in Leydig cells.

PRL_prolactin.effect: stimulates milk production. inhibited by dopamine from hypothalamus. (only anterior pituitary hormone whose default is INHIBITED — all others are stimulated.)

anterior_pituitary.mnemonic: FLAT PiG — FSH, LH, ACTH, TSH, Prolactin, (ignore i), GH

posterior_pituitary.what: neurohypophysis. NOT a true endocrine gland — doesn't make hormones. STORES + RELEASES hormones made by hypothalamus. basically a nerve terminal.

oxytocin.effects: uterine contractions during labor (positive feedback). milk ejection (let-down reflex). bonding, trust, social behavior.

ADH_antidiuretic_hormone.effects: promotes water reabsorption in kidney collecting ducts (aquaporins). raises blood pressure by constricting arterioles at high levels.
ADH_antidiuretic_hormone.hypo: diabetes insipidus — huge volumes of dilute urine. NOT diabetes mellitus.
ADH_antidiuretic_hormone.trigger: released when blood osmolarity rises (dehydration) or blood pressure drops.

thyroid.location: anterior neck. butterfly shape. inferior to larynx, wrapping around trachea.
thyroid.structure: follicles filled with COLLOID (thyroglobulin — the storage form). parafollicular C cells between follicles.

T4_thyroxine.what: major secretory product. 4 iodine atoms. converted to T3 in target tissues. LESS active than T3. longer half-life.
T4_thyroxine.effect: increases BASAL METABOLIC RATE. increases O2 consumption + heat production. critical for growth + development (especially nervous system in fetus/infant).

T3_triiodothyronine.what: 3 iodine atoms. the MORE ACTIVE form. most T3 comes from peripheral conversion of T4.

calcitonin.effect: LOWERS blood Ca2+. inhibits osteoclasts (bone breakdown) + promotes Ca2+ deposition in bone. antagonist of PTH.
calcitonin.note: minor role in adults. more important in children during bone growth.

thyroid.iodine: essential for T3/T4 synthesis. dietary iodine → iodide → trapped by follicular cells → attached to tyrosine residues on thyroglobulin → T3/T4.

disorders.hyper_graves: autoimmune — antibodies mimic TSH → continuous stimulation. symptoms: high BMR, weight loss, heat intolerance, exophthalmos (bulging eyes), nervousness, tachycardia.
disorders.hypo_hashimotos: autoimmune — destroys thyroid tissue. symptoms: low BMR, weight gain, cold intolerance, fatigue, myxedema (puffy face/extremities).
disorders.hypo_infant_cretinism: thyroid deficiency during fetal/infant development → severe intellectual disability + stunted growth. prevented by iodine supplementation + newborn screening.
disorders.goiter: enlarged thyroid. can occur with hyper OR hypo. iodine-deficiency goiter: thyroid enlarges trying to trap more iodine.

parathyroid.location: 4 small glands on POSTERIOR surface of thyroid. (para = beside)

effects: stimulates OSTEOCLASTS → bone resorption → Ca2+ released into blood
activates vitamin D (calcitriol) in kidneys → increases Ca2+ absorption from GI tract
PTH_parathyroid_hormone.hyper: too much PTH → bones weakened (too much resorption), kidney stones (excess Ca2+ in urine).
PTH_parathyroid_hormone.hypo: too little PTH → hypocalcemia → muscle tetany, convulsions (Ca2+ needed for normal nerve/muscle function).

adrenal_glands.location: sit on top of kidneys. suprarenal. two distinct regions.

adrenal_cortex.what: outer region. three zones (from outside in). all make STEROID hormones from cholesterol.

zona_glomerulosa.effect: increases Na+ reabsorption + K+ excretion in kidney → water follows Na+ → blood volume + BP increase.
zona_glomerulosa.regulation: RAAS (renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system). also K+ levels directly.

effects: increases blood glucose (gluconeogenesis — makes glucose from proteins/fats)
zona_fasciculata.regulation: CRH → ACTH → cortisol. negative feedback on hypothalamus + anterior pituitary.

disorders.hyper_cushings: excess cortisol. moon face, buffalo hump, truncal obesity, thin skin, easy bruising, hyperglycemia, muscle wasting, osteoporosis.
disorders.hypo_addisons: cortisol + aldosterone deficiency. fatigue, weight loss, hypotension, hyperpigmentation (excess ACTH stimulates melanocytes), salt craving. JFK had this.

zona_reticularis.effect: converted to testosterone/estrogen in peripheral tissues. contributes to libido, pubic/axillary hair in both sexes. minor compared to gonadal hormones.

adrenal_cortex.layer_mnemonic: GFR = Glomerulosa, Fasciculata, Reticularis. 'the deeper you go, the sweeter it gets' — salt, sugar, sex.

adrenal_medulla.what: inner region. modified sympathetic ganglion. chromaffin cells.
adrenal_medulla.hormones: EPINEPHRINE (80%) + NOREPINEPHRINE (20%). catecholamines. released into BLOOD (hormonal, not neural).
adrenal_medulla.effects: mimics + amplifies sympathetic nervous system — fight or flight response sustained longer because hormones circulate in blood after neural signals stop.
adrenal_medulla.trigger: preganglionic sympathetic fibers directly innervate medulla (ACh → nicotinic receptors on chromaffin cells).

pancreas.what: both EXOCRINE (digestive enzymes into duodenum) + ENDOCRINE (hormones into blood). endocrine portion = ISLETS OF LANGERHANS.

alpha_cells.effects: RAISES blood glucose. stimulates glycogenolysis (glycogen → glucose in liver) + gluconeogenesis (amino acids/fats → glucose).
alpha_cells.mnemonic: think 'gone' — glucose gone from blood, need more

beta_cells.effects: LOWERS blood glucose. promotes glucose uptake into cells (especially muscle + fat). promotes glycogenesis (glucose → glycogen for storage). promotes fat synthesis + protein synthesis.
beta_cells.mnemonic: INsulin lets glucose IN to cells

diabetes_mellitus.type_1: autoimmune destruction of beta cells. NO insulin production. must inject insulin. usually childhood onset. 5-10% of cases.
diabetes_mellitus.type_2: insulin RESISTANCE. cells don't respond to insulin properly. beta cells may eventually burn out. usually adult onset (but increasing in youth). 90-95% of cases. linked to obesity + lifestyle.
diabetes_mellitus.symptoms_3Ps: polyuria (frequent urination), polydipsia (excessive thirst), polyphagia (excessive hunger). also weight loss (type 1), blurred vision, slow healing.

pineal_gland.effects: regulates sleep-wake cycle (circadian rhythm). secretion increases in DARKNESS, decreases in light. peaks at night. may affect reproductive function.
pineal_gland.note: calcifies with age. sometimes visible on X-ray as a midline landmark.

thymus.location: mediastinum (behind sternum). large in childhood, shrinks (involutes) after puberty.
thymus.hormone: THYMOSIN (and other thymic hormones: thymulin, thymopoietin)
thymus.effect: promotes T-LYMPHOCYTE maturation. critical for immune system development. most important in childhood.
thymus.note: by adulthood, mostly replaced by fat. T-cells have already been programmed.

ovaries.estrogen: development of female secondary sex characteristics. menstrual cycle regulation. bone density maintenance.
ovaries.progesterone: prepares + maintains uterine lining for pregnancy. breast development.

testes.testosterone: development of male secondary sex characteristics. sperm production. muscle/bone mass. libido.

gonads.note: regulated by FSH + LH from anterior pituitary (which is regulated by GnRH from hypothalamus).

other_endocrine_tissues.heart: ANP (atrial natriuretic peptide) — released when atria stretched by high blood volume → promotes Na+ + water excretion → lowers BP. antagonist of aldosterone.
other_endocrine_tissues.kidneys: erythropoietin (EPO) — stimulates red blood cell production in bone marrow. released when O2 levels drop. also: renin (enzyme, not hormone — starts RAAS).
other_endocrine_tissues.stomach_intestines: gastrin (stomach acid secretion), secretin (pancreatic bicarbonate), cholecystokinin/CCK (bile + pancreatic enzyme release), GIP (insulin secretion).
other_endocrine_tissues.adipose_tissue: leptin — signals satiety to hypothalamus. more fat = more leptin = less hunger (in theory — obese individuals often have leptin resistance).
other_endocrine_tissues.skin: cholecalciferol (vitamin D3 precursor) — made when UV hits skin → converted to active calcitriol in liver then kidneys → promotes Ca2+ absorption in gut.

calcium_homeostasis_summary.low_Ca2+: PTH released → osteoclasts activated (bone resorption) + kidney reabsorption + vitamin D activation → Ca2+ RISES
calcium_homeostasis_summary.high_Ca2+: calcitonin released → osteoclast inhibition + bone deposition → Ca2+ FALLS
calcium_homeostasis_summary.note: PTH is the major player. calcitonin is relatively minor in adults.

blood_glucose_summary.high_glucose_fed: insulin from beta cells → glucose INTO cells + glycogenesis → glucose FALLS
blood_glucose_summary.low_glucose_fasting: glucagon from alpha cells → glycogenolysis + gluconeogenesis → glucose RISES
blood_glucose_summary.note: cortisol and GH also raise blood glucose (counter-regulatory hormones).
